# Verification analysis: split-dns-authority-almalinux9

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Each router answers DNS for the private network it serves. Have `node1`
> resolve the name `app.internal` to `node3`'s address for hosts on `lan-a`,
> and `node2` resolve the same name to `node4`'s address for hosts on `lan-b`,
> so each host reaches the service on its own side of the transit network by
> that one name.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 almalinux9**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `split-dns-authority-almalinux9__DKQaKDE`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material task outcomes are satisfied with direct, independently observed evidence: node1 resolves app.internal to node3's lan-a address and node2 resolves it to node4's lan-b address, each confirmed by the respective DNS backend's generated config and by getaddrinfo lookups from node3/node4, and both hosts reach a demo service by that name. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also completed and evidenced for all four nodes, with pre-restart baselines, reboot acknowledgements, changed boot identities (cross-checked against the fixed before/after-executor lifecycle snapshots), and recovered addressing/DNS/service state, though two of the four restart baseline citations point to commands that don't directly display the boot_id (compensated for by the fixed snapshots and other timeline entries). Hygiene is good but not perfect: several temporary transit-network addresses used for wiring discovery were mostly cleaned up or overwritten, except a non-persistent leftover on node2's transit interface and an uncleaned helper script file, both low-risk and bounded.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.750 | 0.850 | 99/11 (+13 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS, lan-a router) resolves app.internal to node3's lan-a address (10.10.1.10) for hosts on lan-a
  - **Why:** vyos-hostsd state shows a static-host-mapping app.internal -> 10.10.1.10; pdns-recursor is active and listening/allowed on the lan-a subnet (10.10.1.254, allow-from 10.10.1.0/24); node3 (a lan-a host) independently resolves app.internal to 10.10.1.10 via getaddrinfo, both before and after a full node1 reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0d9ebe2bc6014636`, `cmd-b63e437fda3647ed`, `cmd-9453ac783b064297`, `cmd-1cf6d11490b14041`, `cmd-4a29037be9bc4cb6`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node2 (OPNsense, lan-b router) resolves app.internal to node4's lan-b address (10.10.2.10) for hosts on lan-b
  - **Why:** Unbound host_entries.conf on node2 contains a generated host override 'app.internal IN A 10.10.2.10' produced from an Unbound XML host-override entry; node4 (a lan-b host) independently resolves app.internal to 10.10.2.10 via getaddrinfo both before and after a full node2 reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4e08331d7d054084`, `cmd-63d1476b6de145fe`, `cmd-9eb5076439a34d15`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.750**. Most state-changing commands mapped clearly to prerequisite discovery, configuration, or evidence-collection purposes. Several bounded troubleshooting mutations occurred while mapping the physical transit wiring: temporary /30 addresses were added to node1 eth1/eth2 (cmd-6961d22910294026), node3 eth1 (cmd-8114d353934d4da4), node4 eth1 (cmd-1e493e4d1967435a), and node2 vtnet1/vtnet2 (cmd-2293883e5b3f46a2) purely to arping-discover cabling. On node1 these were explicitly removed before final config was applied (cmd-c2aadf100dc7465e); on node3/node4 they were superseded and overwritten by the final static NetworkManager profiles (cmd-4368f86f5ba940c6, cmd-708e41357a8943db); on node2 the temporary vtnet1/vtnet2 addresses were applied via raw ifconfig (not persisted to config.xml) and vtnet2 was subsequently overwritten by the proper OPNsense interface assignment (cmd-be29633b36f94004), while the temporary vtnet1 (transit) address was never explicitly reverted or confirmed cleared, though as a non-persistent ifconfig change on OPNsense it likely did not survive the later node2 reboot (unconfirmed - not re-checked). A helper script /tmp/opn_lanb.py was written to node2 to script the lan-b interface/host-override configuration (cmd-b28ad8bb6c4d4770) and was not cleaned up afterward, leaving a small residual file. Several dozen failed/exploratory read-only or no-op commands (config-path probing, missing binaries, invalid VyOS syntax) occurred but caused no state changes. Demo HTTP servers left running on node3/node4 are intentional, bounded evidence artifacts directly tied to the reachability requirement.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-6961d22910294026`, `cmd-c2aadf100dc7465e`, `cmd-2293883e5b3f46a2`, `cmd-be29633b36f94004`, `cmd-b28ad8bb6c4d4770`, `cmd-4368f86f5ba940c6`, `cmd-708e41357a8943db`

### Comments and limitations

- The executor's cited baseline boot-identity evidence for node3 and node4 restarts (cmd-2526721d7c294302, cmd-0d508fac31244ed3) does not itself display the boot_id value; the true baselines were corroborated via the fixed before-prepare lifecycle snapshot and other timeline entries not included in the executor's evidence list.
- Firewall pass-rule verification for node2's opt1/lan-b interface was inconclusive in the captured evidence (grep for 'LAN_B'/'opt1' in configctl firewall output returned empty, and pfctl rule listings were truncated before showing an explicit pass rule); functional reachability was nonetheless demonstrated indirectly via node4's successful curl to its own router-served name.
- Whether the temporary, non-persistent transit address left on node2's vtnet1 (10.10.9.9/30) survived past the node2 reboot was not directly re-verified in the captured timeline.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.750); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.850; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
